graphql_authorization.summary: Aimeos disclosed improper GraphQL access control that allowed an editor to manage services through the GraphQL admin API beyond what the corresponding administrative UI permitted.
graphql_authorization.description: The maintainer advisory documents an authorization mismatch in the Aimeos GraphQL administration interface: an editor role can perform service-management operations through GraphQL that are not allowed through the intended JQAdm permission model. The relevant condition is an authenticated GraphQL operation crossing the caller's effective authorization boundary, not schema discovery.
graphql_authorization.selection_basis: official maintainer advisory selected before scoring using WSTG GraphQL and authorization-enforcement semantics

source_map_exposure.summary: IBM DataPower removed access to a JavaScript source map because source maps can be used to read and debug JavaScript files and should not be accessible.
source_map_exposure.description: IBM APAR IT42976 documents an exposed JavaScript source-map artifact in DataPower Gateways. IBM states that JavaScript source maps can be used to help read and debug JavaScript files and that source maps should not be accessible. The relevant evidence is an obtainable debug artifact that exposes readable source information rather than a sourceMappingURL marker alone.
source_map_exposure.selection_basis: fresh official vendor APAR selected before scoring using WSTG-INFO-05 source-map information-leakage semantics

unsafe_api_consumption.summary: HTTP::Tiny forwarded caller-supplied Authorization, Cookie and Proxy-Authorization credentials when following a redirect to a different origin.
unsafe_api_consumption.description: The advisory documents an HTTP client consuming a remote 3xx response and following its Location across scheme, host or port boundaries while re-sending caller-supplied credential headers. The changed redirect destination is therefore trusted without re-applying the original credential boundary, causing Authorization and Proxy-Authorization data to cross to a different host or even an HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrade.
unsafe_api_consumption.selection_basis: fresh upstream-linked advisory selected before scoring using OWASP API10 unsafe-consumption semantics with WSTG-INFO-10 third-party/API trust-boundary mapping

websocket_authorization.summary: Event-Driven Ansible's WebSocket API failed to verify permissions for worker messages, allowing an authenticated user to bypass authorization and receive sensitive credentials for arbitrary activations.
websocket_authorization.description: The vulnerability record describes missing authorization in the Event-Driven Ansible WebSocket endpoint /api/eda/ws/ansible-rulebook. The endpoint does not verify the user's permission for Worker messages, so an authenticated user can forge an arbitrary activation_id and bypass the intended access-control boundary, receiving plaintext OAuth tokens, vault passwords or SSH keys associated with that activation.
websocket_authorization.selection_basis: fresh vendor/CVE source selected before scoring using WSTG WebSocket and authorization-boundary semantics
